# History - Spring AI - Ollama

This example demonstrates how to create a chatbot using a locally hosted large
language model (LLM) with [Ollama](https://ollama.com/). Users can engage in
continuous conversation with the model, asking follow-up questions naturally.
The chat history is saved to a file, allowing the conversation to be resumed at
any time.

Ollama is an open-source platform and command-line tool that enables developers
to download, manage, and run LLMs entirely on local machines, eliminating the
need for cloud APIs, access keys, or privacy-related concerns. It supports
multimodal inputs, tool calling, and integrations with REST and
[Java](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/chat/ollama-chat.html),
making it well-suited for prototyping, debugging, and deploying LLM-powered
applications in a fully offline, customisable environment.

The example uses [Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai), a
Java-based framework for building LLM-enabled applications. It provides tools
for prompt management, call chaining, memory handling, retrieval-augmented
generation (RAG), and integration with external data sources—all within the
Java ecosystem.

[LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j) is an alternative
framework that also offers an abstraction layer between LLMs and the
application.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

## Run the example

1. Download and setup Ollama

   If you haven’t already, please download and install Ollama from the
   [official download page](https://ollama.com/download), following the
   instructions provided. Ollama includes a command-line tool for managing and
   interacting with it.

   Models must be downloaded from a repository, such as the
   [Ollama Library](https://ollama.com/library) or
   [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/models). Ensure the model is saved in
   a supported format, such as
   [GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/gguf).

   To list models installed locally, run:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   After a fresh installation, no models will be listed.

   ```
   NAME    ID    SIZE    MODIFIED
   ```

   To get started, download [LLaMA 3](https://ollama.com/library/llama3) with:

   ```shell
   ollama pull llama3
   ```

   Once the model is downloaded, you can begin using it.

   (*Optional*) To confirm the model has been installed, list the models again:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   You should now see `llama3` in the list.

   ```
   NAME             ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
   llama3:latest    365c0bd3c000    4.7 GB    Less than a second ago
   ```

   To interact with the model using the command-line interface, run:

   ```shell
   ollama run llama3
   ```

   This opens a prompt where you can engage with the model. If the model has not
   yet been downloaded, Ollama will download it automatically. You can interact
   with the model via the CLI

   ```
   >>> When did humans first land on the Moon?

   Humans first landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission. The spacecraft carrying the astronauts, Neil Armstrong and Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin, landed on the lunar surface in the Sea of Tranquility at 20:17 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Armstrong became the first person to set foot on the Moon, famously declaring "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind" as he stepped out of the lunar module Eagle.

   >>> /bye
   ```

   Alternatively, you can interact with the model through a graphical interface,
   such as [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui), which offers
   a web-based experience similar to cloud-hosted models.

   To verify that Ollama is running and accessible on the default port `11434`,
   use:

   ```shell
   curl --silent --show-error 'http://localhost:11434/api/tags' | jq
   ```

   This will return a list of available models.

   ```
   {
     "models": [
       {
         "name": "llama3:latest",
         "model": "llama3:latest",
         "modified_at": "2077-04-27T11:34:56.789000000Z",
         "size": 4661224676,
         "digest": "365c0bd3c000a25d28ddbf732fe1c6add414de7275464c4e4d1c3b5fcb5d8ad1",
         "details": {
           "parent_model": "",
           "format": "gguf",
           "family": "llama",
           "families": [
             "llama"
           ],
           "parameter_size": "8.0B",
           "quantization_level": "Q4_0"
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   When using Ollama via the REST API, as in the following steps, the required
   model must be downloaded in advance. Ollama does not automatically download
   missing models when accessed through the REST API; this functionality is only
   available via the CLI, for example with `ollama run llama3`. Please ensure
   the `llama3` model is available before proceeding.

   Verify that the Ollama APIs can be successfully invoked.

   ```shell
   curl 'http://localhost:11434/api/chat' \
     --silent \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{
     "model": "llama3",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
       }
     ],
     "stream": false,
     "options": {
       "temperature": 0.0
     }
   }' | jq
   ```

   The model response

   ```json
   {
     "model": "llama3",
     "created_at": "2077-04-27T11:35:13.423923598Z",
     "message": {
       "role": "assistant",
       "content": "A historic moment!\n\nHumans first landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, as part of the United States' Apollo 11 mission. NASA astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin \"Buzz\" Aldrin became the first humans to set foot on the lunar surface.\n\nArmstrong stepped out of the lunar module Eagle and onto the Moon's surface at 2:56 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) on July 21, 1969. He famously declared, \"That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind,\" as he took his first steps on the Moon.\n\nAldrin joined Armstrong on the surface about 20 minutes later. The two astronauts spent about two and a half hours on the Moon's surface, collecting samples and conducting experiments.\n\nThe Apollo 11 mission was a historic achievement that marked the first time humans had visited another celestial body. It was a major milestone in space exploration and paved the way for future human spaceflight missions."
     },
     "done": true,
     "done_reason": "stop",
     "total_duration": 16437661702,
     "load_duration": 1360576840,
     "prompt_eval_count": 19,
     "prompt_eval_duration": 366059739,
     "eval_count": 196,
     "eval_duration": 14586339960
   }
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `llama3` model is available. For further details, please refer to Step 1.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --prune --sort=name -L 1 './target'
   ```

   The application JAR file and its dependencies.

   ```
   ./target
   ├── history-springai-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar
   └── history-springai-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar.original

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `llama3` model is available. For further details, please refer to Step 1.

   Run the example.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   The program will start and prints some help information.

   ```
   session> 9b5db82b-daf8-4c35-929a-98804d85c7d4
   Type '/bye' to exit
   Chat with Ollama (through Spring AI) about anything you like. For example
   prompt> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   ---
   prompt>
   ```

   Chat with the model.

   ```
   prompt> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   assistant>
   Humans first landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission. The mission was launched on July 16, 1969, and after traveling through space for four days, the Apollo 11 spacecraft entered into lunar orbit on July 19. The next day, July 20, astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin descended to the Moon's surface in the Lunar Module Eagle, while Michael Collins remained in orbit around the Moon in the Command Module Columbia. At 20:17 UTC (6:17 PM EDT), Armstrong became the first person to set foot on the Moon, famously declaring "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind" as he stepped out of the Eagle onto the Moon's surface.
   prompt> Where did they land?
   assistant>
   The Apollo 11 mission landed on the Moon in the Sea of Tranquility, which is located in the eastern hemisphere of the Moon. Specifically, the Lunar Module Eagle landed in the lunar surface coords 0°37' N latitude and 23°25' E longitude, at an altitude of about 40 km (25 miles) above the Moon's surface. The landing site is also known as "Harrison Schmitt Station" after the mission's lunar module pilot, Harrison Schmitt, who became the first person to touch the Moon's surface after Armstrong and Aldrin.
   prompt> From where did they launch?
   assistant>
   The Apollo 11 mission launched from Kennedy Space Center on Merritt Island, Florida, USA. The launch site was designated as "Launch Complex 39" (LC-39), and the spacecraft was carried aloft by a Saturn V rocket. The launch took place at 20:07 UTC (4:07 PM EDT) on July 16, 1969, and the spacecraft entered into orbit around the Earth before traveling to the Moon.
   prompt>
   ```

   You can type `/bye` to exit.

   Notice how the model appears to recall previous interactions. However, the
   model itself is stateless; Spring AI manages this through conversation
   history.
